title: Regional weighted placement and graceful eviction policy for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a regional weighted placement and graceful eviction policy for Dedicated capacity that balances throughput guarantees, autoscaling responsiveness, and strict data residency constraints. The goal is to provide deterministic placement decisions for customer pools while supporting non-disruptive rebalancing (eviction/drain) when capacity is constrained or when topology changes (zone maintenance, scale-down, failover). This ticket covers the placement algorithm, eviction orchestration, residency lock enforcement, and integration points with autoscaler and billing/quotas systems.
acceptance_criteria: Placement engine exposes a region/zone weight configuration per dedicated-pool and honors per-customer residency locks at allocation time
Scaling operations (up/down) maintain throughput guarantees for pinned pools and provide preemptive reservations for high-SLO customers
Graceful eviction sequence implemented: notify, slow-drain, migrate KV/prefix cache where applicable, handoff sessions, and verify <1% failed requests for affected pools during routine rebalances
Automated rollback path if latency or error rates exceed configured thresholds during eviction
Audit logs capture region-of-allocation and eviction reason for every slot reassignment (for compliance)
tasks: Design placement policy schema (weights, soft/hard affinity, residency-lock TTLs) — API and control-plane contract
Prototype weighted placement scheduler in simulator and run traffic replays to validate throughput distribution
Implement eviction choreography in orchestrator with drain phases and health-check gating
Integrate with autoscaler to respect buffer reservations for P0/P1 customers
Add audit log fields and surface residency metrics in Console
Create e2e test harness simulating zone failures, maintenance windows, and scale-down events
Performance benchmark: ensure p95 latency regression <5% for steady workloads during rebalances
progress_updates: 2025-11-14: Kickoff meeting with Product and SRE. Agreed on weight vs affinity semantics and the need for both soft and hard residency locks.
2025-12-02: Simulator prototype completed. Initial run with production traces shows weighted placement achieves 92% of desired throughput distribution across regions under churn.
2026-01-08: Draft API schema posted to Confluence (link below). Feedback requested from Security on audit fields for residency compliance.

2026-01-22: Implemented eviction choreography MVP in dev-orchestrator branch. Observed a window of increased tail latency when moving KV-heavy workloads — introduced staged drain and KV checkpointing to mitigate.
2026-02-15: Integration test with autoscaler shows buffer reservations prevent loss of throughput for pinned pools during neighbor scale-downs. Need to tune reservation decay for bursty workloads.

2026-03-04: Canary rollout in us-west with two customers. Measured <0.6% error spike and p95 latency +3% during a scheduled zone rotation. Monitoring dashboards updated; continuing observation before broader rollout.
review_feedback: PM (Elena Zhou): Prefer explicit per-customer residency override rather than only pool-level to support enterprise compliance cases.
SRE (Mark Rivers): Add circuit-breaker to abort eviction if downstream caches report >5% key-miss amplification; otherwise risk cascading load.
Security (Riona Gupta): Audit trail must include the requesting principal and decision path for legal discovery. Also recommend HSM-backed signing of residency assertions for Private deployments.
UX (Design) — informal: Console should show expected post-placement capacity heatmap and estimated impact window before triggering manual evictions.
notes: Trade-offs: hard residency locks increase fragmentation and reduce global bin-packing efficiency; mitigations include TTL-based soft locks and preemptive migration windows.
We intentionally decoupled weight assignment from autoscaler decisions so product teams can set regional priorities independently of cost-driven scaling.
Eviction is two-phase: (1) soft-drain where existing requests finish and new requests are routed to fallback model variants; (2) forced-reassign for nodes that fail health checks after grace period.
Next steps: extend simulator to include cost modeling and run 1,000 synthetic customer profiles to find pathological cases for reservation sizing.
